$comment: Library surface materials, themes and tint swatches (map/materials.ts; maps, tiles, themes and Style Packs name a material or theme by `id`, so never rename or remove one). `materials` is MapMaker's palette order. A material is a procedural `pattern` (its painter is code: packages/client/src/materials/patterns.ts) in `base` and `accent` (#rrggbb), or a scanned `texture` set (content/textures.json: textures/<id>_color.jpg and _normal.jpg, _emission.jpg when `emissive`; `base` is its average colour, for minimaps and icons). `scale`: metres one repeat covers; `shine`: 0 matte to 1 glossy; `emissive`: glows whatever the light. A theme gives each surface slot (floor, walls, solids, underside, trim) its default `material` and optional `tint`, the `sky` colour, and its matching Ground theme (`ground`). A Ground theme (`groundThemes`, ids `ground.*`; docs/MAPMAKER_PAINTING_PLAN.md, Phase 4) is the base ground every unpainted terrain cell shows (`base`), the grounds MapMaker's Ground paint offers first (`grounds`, the base first) and the Structure themes it suits (`suits`: every theme whose match it is, and any others); all are ground materials (the Ground category, or a terrain layer of before map format v45: Mossy Rock, Hex Paving). The v45 migration makes a map's most common old layer that is some Ground theme's base the map's base (the first such theme, in this order), so keep the order and a theme for each layer shipped maps lean on. No network code: materials and themes travel as their id inside the map. Edit, then run `node tools/content/materials.mjs`.

notes.design: One repeat is 5 m: two bays 2.5 m wide and one 5 m deep, lines 12 cm wide. Lay it on a floor or a block; the lines follow the world grid, not the cell.
Slabs 0.4 m square with 6 × 6 studs: the warning strip at a kerb, a crossing or a platform edge. Tint it for the buff or red kinds.

One storey (4 m) a repeat, the paint across the middle of it. Abstract shapes only (a cloud, a bolt, a wave, a zigzag scribble, dots, a ring, runs of paint): no letters, words, logos or real marks. Base: the brick; accent: the mortar.
Painted plaster fallen away in ragged patches to the brick behind, grey undercoat round each patch. Base: the plaster; accent: the brick.
